page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.large is a virtual computing instance operating on KVM hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading. The instance includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions such as AVX and AVX-512F, along with AES cryptography acceleration. The system is provisioned with 8.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and contains no local disk storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage for operational workloads.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.n1.large in the entry-level performance bracket. In CPU-bound workloads, the instance achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1106.18 and a multi-core score of 4400.61, both ranking in the bottom quartile. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 929.0 and a multi-core score of 2969.0. Memory throughput metrics show a read-only large-block bandwidth of 34.59 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 29.39 GB/sec, placing write memory performance in the middle tier. In data handling and serving benchmarks, the configuration achieves 5.51 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.41 GB/sec of static web throughput.

Given its hardware constraints and legacy processing tier, the ecs.n1.large represents an economical choice for utility operations that do not require high memory density or sustained high-clock execution. The absence of local solid-state storage requires reliance on network block devices, making it less suitable for high-frequency transactional databases. Appropriate deployment scenarios include lightweight background workers, small-scale web servers, dev-test environments, and low-concurrency automation tasks.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.large is an entry-tier virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the configuration delivers 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance contains zero local NVMe or SSD storage and includes no dedicated graphics hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic performance benchmarks reflect baseline processing capabilities, with a single-core Geekbench score of 929.0 and 5.51 million Redis SET operations per second. With modest compute throughput and unbundled disk volumes, the ecs.n1.large is suited for low-traffic web services, background utilities, orchestration workers, and non-critical development and test deployments.
